title: Development and Validation of Automated Methods for the Evaluation of Speech Audiometric Tests Compared with Standard Clinical Methods
summary:
Background: Speech tests are an important part of hearing assessment. At present, spoken responses often need to be evaluated by trained personnel. The aim of this project is to develop a system that can perform this evaluation automatically.

Research question: The study investigates whether automated methods provide results comparable to current clinical procedures and whether they are suitable for routine clinical use.

Methods: The project consists of three study parts. First, speech recordings obtained during routine speech tests are collected to develop and improve the automated evaluation. Second, the developed method is compared with current clinical procedures. Finally, a dedicated hardware device with integrated automated evaluation is assessed under practical conditions. The study includes normal-hearing participants as well as participants with hearing impairment.
conditions: Hearing impairment (including cochlear implant users) and normal hearing as a control group

interventions.name: Prospective observational study consisting of three consecutive study parts. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Written informed consent.
- For study part 1: Routine speech audiometric examination in open response mode and consent to recording of spoken responses.
- For study parts 2 and 3:
*Sufficient German language skills to perform the speech audiometric tests.
*either normal hearing (pure-tone average at 500 Hz, 1 kHz, 2 kHz and 4 kHz ≤ 25 dB HL), or unilateral or bilateral hearing impairment.
Exclusion criteria:
- Age < 18 years.
- No written informed consent.
- For study part 1: No consent to recording of spoken responses.
- For study parts 2 and 3: 
*Insufficient German language skills to perform the speech audiometric tests.
*Participants who cannot be assigned to one of the predefined study groups (normal hearing or hearing impairment).
